thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert fired for P1 - edge: LB target health + TLS handshake surge

mike.h: acked and taking. grabbing logs and checking LB health.

sara.ops: seeing client TLS resets from eu-west-1, lots of "connection reset by peer" in proxy. multiple customers reporting timeouts. tagging @cs-team @support.

jordan.net: ALB health shows 4 of 15 targets unhealthy in eu-west-1 (gpu-pool-eu). spike in TLS errors starting ~2026-03-15T06:10Z. sample from proxy logs: `tls: handshake failure`, `remote error: internal_error`.

oncall-1: PD notes auto-retry tried failover but thresholds didn't kick (health < failover threshold). PD escalated when error rate hit 7% across region.

mike.h: any recent infra changes in eu? cert rotations, OpenSSL updates?

jordan.net: kernel/openssl patch rolled to gpu pools at 02:00Z earlier this morning as part of routine security rollout. eu pool was included. I see a mismatch in enabled ciphers between edge proxy and worker nginx. suspect negotiation fallback is failing.

sara.ops: impact summary so far: ~15% request failures for generate/chat endpoints in EU over last 12m. internal incident severity P1. notifying CS + execs.

mike.h: starting mitigation: shifting traffic weights away from gpu-pool-eu to gpu-pool-global to reduce failed handshakes. will also enable additional TLS ciphers on proxies as temporary measure.

mike.h: executing weight change:
```
# infractl
infractl route edit --region eu-west-1 --service edge --set-weight gpu-pool-eu:0,gpu-pool-global:100
```

eng-sre-bot: weight change accepted; connection drain in progress. active conns to gpu-pool-eu down 60% in 90s. gpu-pool-global p99 latency up 10% but within SLO.

jordan.net: enabling fallback ciphers on edge proxies now (short lived) to accept older handshakes:
```
# on proxy
nginx: ssl_ciphers HIGH:!aNULL:!MD5:TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256:TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384
```

mike.h: quick host check on one unhealthy target shows OpenSSL 1.1.1 -> worker nginx built against openssl1.1 and the proxy expects TLSv1.3-only handshake. restarting nginx with compatible cipher list on affected hosts.

mike.h: restart done on gpu-eu-07, target rejoined healthy set. rolling restart queued for gpu-eu-04 and gpu-eu-12.

incident-bot: PagerDuty: Auto-escalation to SRE lead (assigned to sara.ops).

sara.ops: taking lead. coordinating mitigation and comms. preliminary root cause hypothesis: package rollout (openssl/kernel) changed available cipher suites and server config drift left some workers incompatible with the proxy's stricter TLS profile.

mike.h: health metrics after weight shifts and restarts: unhealthy target count down to 0/15 in eu-west-1 within 8 minutes, TLS error rate dropped from 7% -> 0.8%.

emily.cs: CS update drafted and sent to impacted customers: "We observed TLS handshake errors affecting customers in EU; traffic was rerouted and affected hosts restarted. Full mitigation in progress; we will follow up with timeline and root cause."

support: routing inbound customer tickets to priority queue; collecting customer request IDs for investigation.

jordan.net: next steps (action items): 1) add TLS compatibility check to post-deploy CI for edge/worker stacks, 2) add automated cipher matrix test during canary rollout, 3) review package rollout process to catch config drift, 4) lower failover PD threshold to 25% (current 30%). filing infra tickets now.

oncall-1: filing PD threshold adjust request: INFRA-7892.

eng-sre-bot: quick dashboards: grafana link https://grafana.internal/redwood/edge-tls/alerts showing request error and target health timelines.

mike.h: good mitigation. recommend keeping the temporary cipher fallback for 1–2 hours while restarts finish, then revert and monitor. planning 24h post-incident monitoring window.

sara.ops: agreed. i'll lead post-incident doc and assign owners: PR hotfix for worker nginx config (owner: mike.h), CI canary TLS test (owner: jordan.net), customer follow-up (owner: emily.cs).

incident-bot: PagerDuty: all incidents acknowledged. will resolve when oncall marks resolved.

mike.h: marking incident resolved in channel after 30m of stable metrics.

sara.ops: closing out thread for live mitigation; moving to incident-postmortem channel for write-up. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
